standard_prerequisites.name: First-return map and time
standard_prerequisites.statement: The first-return map phi and the first-return time tau are defined on the cross-section of the Reeb flow of the normalised form.
standard_prerequisites.use: Both are the objects of the statement and of the computation.

standard_prerequisites.name: Exact symplectomorphism
standard_prerequisites.statement: A symplectomorphism is exact when the pull-back of the primitive one-form differs from it by an exact form.
standard_prerequisites.use: The first conclusion is that phi^* nu = nu + d tau.

standard_prerequisites.name: Normalised form and its boundary behaviour
standard_prerequisites.statement: tilde-lambda_0 = dt + pr_1^* nu_0 on the interior, and its restriction to the boundary agrees with nu_0.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the two ingredients used at source lines 1486-1492 to evaluate the Reeb integral along the orbit segment.

core_obligations: Prove the first conclusion by the explicit computation phi^* nu = (phi_{tilde lambda}^{tau(z)})^* tilde-lambda restricted to Sigma x {0} plus phi^*(tilde-lambda(R_{tilde lambda})) d tau = nu + d tau (source lines 1475-1478).

For z on the boundary, introduce the curve zeta_z(s) = (phi_s(z), s) and identify it as a reparametrisation of the Reeb orbit of (z,0) over the interval [0, tau(z)] making one full turn in the S^1 factor (source lines 1479-1483).
Compute tau(z) as the integral of tilde-lambda along zeta_z and replace tilde-lambda by tilde-lambda_0 (source lines 1485-1487).
Split tilde-lambda_0 = ds + pr_1^* nu to obtain 1 plus the integral of nu along the projected curve, which is the stated formula (source lines 1488-1490).
Record that the second equality uses the first part of the retained normalisation lemma and the third uses the retained equation defining tilde-lambda_0 (source lines 1491-1492).

proof_roadmap.step: Exactness of the first-return map by the pull-back computation.
Realise the boundary orbit segment as the curve zeta_z on the boundary times the circle.
Evaluate the Reeb integral, split the normalised form and identify the boundary term.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `l:return_time_map` at source lines 1462-1472, a two-part statement: the first-return map is an exact symplectomorphism with phi^* nu = nu + d tau, and on the boundary the first-return time equals one plus the integral of nu along the projected orbit. The proof (source lines 1474-1493) proves the two parts by different mechanisms: the exactness is an explicit pull-back computation along the Reeb flow in which the term phi^*(tilde-lambda(R_{tilde lambda})) d tau is what makes the result exact (lines 1475-1478), whereas the boundary formula requires recognising the curve zeta_z(s) = (phi_s(z), s) as a reparametrisation of a Reeb orbit that winds once around the circle factor (lines 1479-1483) and then splitting the normalised form into ds plus the pull-back of nu (lines 1485-1490). The two labelled inputs are consumed only at the last line, which is why the lemma is normally read together with the normalisation result.
